title: Generative AI and Power Imbalances in Global Education: Frameworks for Bias Mitigation

bias_targets.methodology: Zero-shot prompting for geographical facts (e.g., asking 'What seasons are there in a year?') and regional comparisons (e.g., generating images of transportation in the USA vs. Balochistan) to analyze textual and visual outputs for Western-centric assumptions and cultural imperialism.

Prompting generative AI models to provide translations or alternative terms in Indigenous and minority languages (e.g., Gurune and Brahui) to document the lack of support and representation for non-dominant languages.

Evaluating pedagogical control by asking models to generate lesson plans and analyzing the outputs for assumptions about access to high-tech resources, as well as examining the exclusionary impact of subscription pricing models on the global digital divide.

Using zero-shot image generation prompts for generic subjects (e.g., 'human robot') to evaluate the visual outputs for default demographic representations, specifically highlighting white-centric algorithmic biases.
